A three-year [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) veteran, he last played for the [[Orlandina Basket]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] and played [[College basketball|collegiate basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. ==High school career== Flynn and [[Niagara Falls High School]] won the 2005 New York state public high school and federation championships. He was also named [[Mr. New York Basketball|New York State Mr. Basketball]] following his senior year. When he graduated with the class of 2007, he was ranked the No. 22 overall recruit and No. 4 point guard by Rivals.com as well as the No. 23 overall and the No. 4 point guard by Scout.com. Flynn was a 2007 [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and he was named to the 2007 USA Basketball Junior National Select Team that competed against the World Select Team in the 10th annual Nike Hoop Summit in Memphis, Tennessee. Flynn was a former high school and college teammate of guard/forward [[Paul Harris (basketball)|Paul Harris]], whom he played alongside as members of the Minnesota Timberwolves' summer league team. In his senior year, Flynn averaged 26.7 points, 6.0 assists, 3.5 steals and 3.3 rebounds. In 2009 as ''[[The Buffalo News]]'' celebrated 50 years of All-[[Western New York]] (WNY) basketball selections, Flynn, who was twice an All-WNY first team selection was a third team selection for the All-time All-WNY team along with [[Gary Bossert]], [[Jason Rowe (basketball)|Jason Rowe]], Aaron Curry, and Jimmy "Bug" Williams.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/381940241|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|381940241}}|title=All-time All-WNY team: How'd we do?|work=[[The Buffalo News]]|author=McShea, Keith|accessdate=February 9, 2024|date=March 7, 2009|page=|quote=First team Curtis Aiken, Bennett 1981-82, '82-83 Paul Harris, Niagara Falls, 2003-04, '04-05 Christian Laettner, Nichols 1986-87, '87-88 Bob Lanier, Bennett 1965-66 Mel Montgomery, Kensington 1969-70, '70-71 Second team Ritchie Campbell, Burgard 1988-89, '89-90 George Carter, Silver Creek 1960-61, '61-62 Mike Russell, East 1973-74 Dwight Williams, Neumann 1974-75 Tim Winn, LaSalle 1993-94, '94-95, '95-96 Third team Gary Bossert, Kenmore West 1981-82, '82-83 Aaron Curry, Neumann 1975-76 Jonny Flynn, Niagara Falls, 2005-06, '06-07 Jason Rowe, Traditional 1993-94, '94-95, '95-96 Jimmy "Bug" Williams, East 1971-72, '72-73}}{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/464904948|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|464904948}}|title=WNY's all-time high school basketball team|publisher=[[McClatchy]]-[[Tribune Content Agency|Tribune Business News]]|author=McShea, Keith|accessdate=February 9, 2024|date=March 7, 2009|page=|quote=Our staff has been banging under the boards for more than a month, picking our all-decade teams as we built toward this point, the final shot of our celebration of the 50th anniversary of All-WNY basketball. . .There were letters, e-mails, voice mails, blog comments and phone calls. There were opinions from coaches, teammates, fathers, brothers, sons and of course fans.}} ==College career== ===2007–08=== In his first game ever, on November 12, 2007, Flynn scored 28 points, which eclipsed former Orange standout [[Carmelo Anthony]]'s record for most points in a freshman's debut.[https://web.archive.org/web/20220407164851/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/273160183 Freshman Flynn sets pace as Syracuse holds off Siena] Later in the season, he matched his debut performance with another 28-point effort in an 82–77 loss to [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]] on March 21, 2008.[https://web.archive.org/web/20170823204406/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=280610183 Pittsburgh snags fifth straight win at Syracuse] Flynn would go on to have a prolific freshman year, collecting co-[[Big East]] Rookie of the Year honors, with averages of 15.7 points and 5.3 assists per game. Flynn and fellow freshman [[Donté Greene]] were the second-highest-scoring freshman duo in the country, combining to average 33.4 points per outing. ===2008–09=== Flynn was named to the preseason All Big East team{{Cite web |url=http://www.bigeast.org/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=19400&ATCLID=1605721 |title=Archived copy |access-date=January 7, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090204033402/http://www.bigeast.org/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=19400 |archive-date=February 4, 2009 |url-status=dead }} and started the season with a 27-point effort against [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond]] on November 18, 2008.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=283230183 Richmond Spiders vs. Syracuse Orange – Box Score – November 18, 2008 – ESPN] Seven days later, Flynn scored 25 points and hit a 3-pointer with 6.4 seconds left in regulation as Syracuse defeated then-No. 23 ESPN/USA Today, No. 22 AP [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] 89–81 in overtime in the championship game of the CBE Classic. Flynn was named MVP of the Tournament.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=283230183 Kansas Jayhawks vs. Syracuse Orange – Recap – November 25, 2008 – ESPN] Flynn's leaping ability was on display in a January 11, 2009, game against [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]]. With Syracuse clinging to a 52–48 lead, Flynn drove to the hoop and threw down a monstrous dunk over opposing guard Michael Rosario as he attempted to draw a charge.[http://syracuse.scout.com/a.z?s=185&p=2&c=829345 Scout.com: Flynn's dunk slams Rutgers chances][http://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/index.ssf/2009/01/as_they_play_11_syracuse_vs_ru.html As They Played: No. 11 Syracuse vs. Rutgers | NJ.com][http://media.www.dailyorange.com/media/storage/paper522/news/2008/12/05/Sports/Mbb-GameChanger.Flynns.HighFlying.Dunk.Lifts.Syracuse.To.Win.Over.Rutgers-3583066.shtml MBB | GAME-CHANGER: Flynn's high-flying dunk lifts Syracuse to win over Rutgers – Sports – The Daily Orange] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090116042352/http://media.www.dailyorange.com/media/storage/paper522/news/2008/12/05/Sports/Mbb-GameChanger.Flynns.HighFlying.Dunk.Lifts.Syracuse.To.Win.Over.Rutgers-3583066.shtml |date=January 16, 2009 }}[http://web.sny.tv/news/article.jsp?ymd=20090110&content_id=1487570&oid=2&vkey=21 Flynn's dunk spurs 'Cuse win at Rutgers | SNY.tv: News] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090319002233/http://web.sny.tv/news/article.jsp?ymd=20090110&content_id=1487570&oid=2&vkey=21 |date=March 19, 2009 }} In the quarterfinals of the 2009 [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] on March 12 and 13, Flynn led the Orange to a 127–117 win in six overtimes over the favored [[University of Connecticut|Connecticut]] [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|Huskies]]. Flynn played 67 out of a possible 70 minutes on the floor that evening, leading the Orange by scoring 34 points, adding 11 assists and making all 16 of his free throw attempts.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game?gameId=290710041 College Basketball Gamecast – Syracuse vs Connecticut]{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/03/13/sports/ncaabasketball/13uconn.html| work=The New York Times | title=Syracuse Left Standing After Marathon Game | first=Pete | last=Thamel |authorlink=Pete Thamel | date=March 13, 2009 | access-date=May 7, 2010}} The next day, Flynn then played all 45 minutes of Syracuse's 74–69 overtime victory over [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] in the Big East semifinals. He scored 15 points and had 9 assists.{{cite news| url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2009/03/14/syracuse-winssemifinal | work=CNN | title='Marathon Men' advance to final | date=March 14, 2009 | access-date=April 5, 2023}} Syracuse, however, would eventually fall to [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] in the Big East championship game, 76–66. For his efforts, Flynn was named the 2009 Big East tournament's MVP, the fourth player from the losing team to win the award in the tournament's history.{{cite news| url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/2009/03/14/2009-03-14_jonny_flynn_gets_big_east_mvp_nod.html | location=New York | work=Daily News | title=Jonny Flynn gets Big East MVP nod | first=Matt | last=Gagne | date=March 15, 2009}} In his first career [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] game in 2009, Flynn led all scorers in their first-round matchup against [[Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks basketball|Stephen F. Austin]], tallying 16 points and 7 assists. Syracuse went on to win the game 59–44. On March 22, 2009, Flynn scored 11 points and add 7 assists as Syracuse defeated [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] 78–67 advancing Syracuse to its first Sweet Sixteen since 2004.[https://web.archive.org/web/20181120095353/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=294000040 Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks vs. Syracuse Orange – NCAA Tournament Game – Recap – March 20, 2009 – ESPN] On April 9, 2009, it was announced by Syracuse University that Flynn would declare himself eligible for the upcoming [[2009 NBA draft|NBA draft]]. However, Flynn would retain his [[NCAA]] eligibility by not immediately hiring an agent.{{cite web|url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2009/04/syracuses_jonny_flynn_eric_dev.html|title=Syracuse's Jonny Flynn, Eric Devendorf and Paul Harris will enter the NBA draft|access-date=April 9, 2009|date=April 9, 2009|first=Mike|last=Waters}} Flynn officially decided to forgo his final two years at Syracuse and signed with Creative Artists Agency Sports, run by [[Sports agent|agent]] [[Leon Rose]], on April 15.{{cite web|url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orange-segment/2009/04/interview_with_jonny_flynn_syr.html|title=Interview with Jonny Flynn: Syracuse basketball star officially signs an agent|first=Ryan|last=Miller|access-date=April 15, 2009|date=April 15, 2009}} He was ultimately drafted sixth overall by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2009–2011)=== Flynn was drafted sixth overall in the [[2009 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], notably just one selection ahead of future two-time [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award|MVP]] [[Stephen Curry]] at the [[point guard]] position. Expectations were very high for Flynn as he was seen as the future cornerstone point guard for the Timberwolves by GM [[David Kahn (sports executive)|David Kahn]]. Flynn's stats were solid for his rookie season: he averaged 13.5 points per game and 4.4 assists per game.{{Cite web |title=Jonny Flynn Career Stats - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/3985/jonny-flynn |access-date=2024-02-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}} On October 28, 2009, Flynn made his professional debut and sparked a rally for the Timberwolves, coming back from 19 points down. Flynn scored 13 points in the 4th quarter to lead the Timberwolves to a victory over the [[New Jersey Nets]].[https://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5hFVhxDqNHIz0_o9sKsqqjzMWxgJQD9BKGIV80 Flynn rallies Timberwolves over Nets]{{dead link|date=June 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}. Retrieved on November 4, 2009. On December 14, 2009, he made the driving game-winning layup to beat the [[Utah Jazz]] 110–108, scoring 28 points.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120909223819/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2009/12/15/SPJ31B4AHF.DTL|title=Flynn and Wolves like to run and win to the sound of Jazz}}. Retrieved on December 16, 2009. On January 18, 2010, he set a new career high with 29 points against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in a 108–103 overtime victory.[https://www.bostonherald.com/2010/01/19/jonny-flynn-keys-minnesota-comeback Jonny Flynn keys Minnesota comeback] At the end of the season, Flynn was selected to the All-Rookie second team. On January 31, 2010, Flynn had a career-high eight rebounds in a 112–91 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{Cite web|title=New York Knicks at Minnesota Timberwolves Box Score, January 31, 2010|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201001310MIN.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=2020-05-17}} Flynn underwent hip surgery during the summer of 2010.[http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2010/07/27/minnesotas-jonny-flynn-has-hip-surgery-will-miss-start-of-the-season/ Minnesota's Jonny Flynn has hip surgery, will miss start of the season] This surgery caused Flynn's decline in production and play. His [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11]] campaign was widely considered to be a disappointment, as his numbers dipped to 5.3 points per game and only 3.4 assists per game. This led to much speculation of his departure following the season.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/players/4611/career;_ylt=AlIRZ9nPw6bn_bqqlL29w9.kvLYF Jonny Flynn – Houston Rockets – Career Statistics – NBA – Yahoo! Sports] On March 2, 2011, Flynn dropped a career-high 14 assists in a 116–105 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web|title=Minnesota Timberwolves at Detroit Pistons Box Score, March 2, 2011|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201103020DET.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=2020-05-17}} === Houston Rockets (2011–2012) === During the [[2011 NBA draft]], Flynn was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]], along with [[Donatas Motiejūnas]], in exchange for [[Brad Miller (basketball)|Brad Miller]], the number 23 and 38 picks in the draft, and a future first-round draft pick. The number 23 pick became [[Nikola Mirotić]] and the number 38 pick became [[Chandler Parsons]]. === Portland Trail Blazers (2012) === On March 15, 2012, Flynn was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], along with [[Hasheem Thabeet]] and a future second-round pick ([[Will Barton]] was later selected), for [[Marcus Camby]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7691515 Houston Rockets have deal to acquire Marcus Camby, sources say – ESPN] === Melbourne Tigers (2012–2013) === On October 1, 2012, Flynn signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]].[http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-add-terrence-williams-and-jonny-flynn-training-camp-roster Detroit Pistons Add Terrence Williams and Jonny Flynn to Training Camp Roster] On October 22, 2012, Flynn was waived by the Pistons.[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/224097/Pistons_Waive_Flynn_Terrence_Williams Pistons Waive Flynn, Terrence Williams] On November 5, 2012, Flynn signed with the [[Melbourne Tigers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]].{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130403222421/http://www.skynews.com.au/sport/article.aspx?id=813071|title=Tigers sign NBA player Johnny Flynn}} In his first game in the NBL, and after only a few days of preparation, Flynn was impressive with 12 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, and one block and lifted the struggling Tigers to a dominant 96–66 win over the [[Adelaide 36ers]].[http://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/basketball/melbournes-flynn-factor-overpowers-sixers/story-fnanosvn-1226514028491 Jonny Flynn sends shudders through NBL in Tigers debut] Flynn continued to have an impact on the NBL and, following an injury to [[Kevin Lisch]], was selected as the substitute starting point guard for the South All-Stars in their 134–114 win over the North All-Stars in the [[2012 NBL All-Star Game]] held at the [[Titanium Security Arena|Adelaide Arena]] on December 22, 2012. In 19:56 of game time, Flynn recorded seven points, five rebounds and ten assists.[http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/basketball/south-down-north-in-nbl-all-star-contest-at-adelaide-arena/story-fndekpx4-1226542349438 South down North in NBL All Star contest at Adelaide Arena] Flynn joined the [[Indiana Pacers]] for the 2013 [[NBA Summer League|Orlando Summer League]].[http://www.hoopsworld.com/indiana-pacers-2013-orlando-summer-league-roster Indiana Pacers 2013 Orlando Summer League Roster] He then joined the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the [[NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]].[http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-announce-summer-league-roster CLIPPERS ANNOUNCE SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER] After the [[2013 NBA Summer League]] ended, Flynn left the NBA and never returned. ===Orlandina (2014–2015)=== In September 2013, Flynn joined the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/229933/Jonny-Flynn-Signs-With-Sichuan-Blue-Whales-Of-China Jonny Flynn Signs With Sichuan Blue Whales Of China][http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/63667/jonny-flynn-signs-in-china-with-sichuan-blue-whales.html Jonny Flynn signs in China with Sichuan Blue Whales] However, he left a month later due to injury.[http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/65362/jonny-flynn-reportedly-leaves-sichuan-due-to-injury.html Jonny Flynn reportedly leaves Sichuan due to injury] On August 30, 2014, Flynn signed with [[Orlandina Basket]] of Italy for the 2014–15 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/133042/orlandina-officially-signs-jonny-flynn.html Orlandina officially signs Jonny Flynn] On November 24, 2014, he parted ways with Orlandina, after playing only two games in [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]] before getting injured.{{cite news|title=Jonny Flynn, Orlandina part ways|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/142409/jonny-flynn-orlandina-part-ways.html|access-date=November 24, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=November 24, 2014}} ==National team career== Flynn was named as a 2006 USA Men's U18 National Team member on June 26, 2006, at the 2006 FIBA Americas U18 Championship for men in [[San Antonio]], [[Texas]]. During the tournament, he averaged 8.5 points, 3.8 rebounds, a team-high 5.3 assists, and 1.8 steals per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/biosmen/johnny_flynn_bio.html |title=USA Basketball: Bio |access-date=June 11, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070312151954/http://www.usabasketball.com/biosmen/johnny_flynn_bio.html |archive-date=March 12, 2007 }} Flynn would once again play on Team USA in the 2007 USA Basketball U19 World Championships. The team took home the silver medal, as Flynn averaged 9.6 points per game in the USA's nine games.{{Cite web |url=http://carrierdome.syr.edu/news/basketball/mbasket/2007/7/22/USA19U7.22.07.asp?path=mbasket%3Fpath%3Dmbasket |title=Archived copy |access-date=August 10, 2007 |archive-date=May 27, 2007
